### **A Letter of Sympathy to the President of the United States**

  
The other day, I watched a few posts online  
mocking you as you winced at the deafening sound  
of a military jet flying over your head.  
I didn't like the tone of many of those posts.  
I don't blame you for such a reaction.  
I have reacted like this, and worse, hundreds of times.  
My parents, wife, kids, and siblings have too.  
So all of us now  
know how  
that sound feels.

In 2008, I was 16  
on the roof of our house in Beit Lahia,  
standing with my father, watching his pigeons in their coop,  
when an Israeli, U.S.-made F-16  
flew low, like a shaving machine,  
before razing a neighborhood.

I panicked at its piercing shriek,

but also at the sight of the missiles

mounted beneath its wings.

But Mr. President, all of us, except you, know  
the screech of a missile  
or the blast of an explosion.  
Do you know what's louder than the screech and the blast?

The voice of a mother in Jabalia Camp,  
begging me on October 31, 2023,  
to search for the bodies of her husband and children  
under the rubble  
not just of her house,  
but of the entire neighborhood.

The desperate pleas of 5-year-old Hind Rajab  
from her uncle's car in January 2024,  
and the 335 bullets fired at her  
before, during, and after the call.

The trickle of tears on the cheek of a father  
who returned with no bread for his kids in a tent  
in Khan Younis, and the screams of an infant  
whose mother's breast had dried up.

The heartbeat of 18-year-old Ahed  
as her uncle, Dr. Hani Bseiso,  
amputated her leg on a kitchen table,

without anesthesia.

It was dark!

The grinding footsteps of Dr. Hussam Abu Safiyya  
as he walked toward the tank in his white coat.

I can hear the sound of his disappearance.

And I can still hear and hear more!

But do you know what will be much louder than all?

The sound of the gavel  
in the court of justice.

 _**Mosab Abu Toha** is a Palestinian poet and writer from Gaza. He won the
2025 Pulitzer Prize for commentary and the 2024 OPC's Flora Lewis Award and
was a finalist for the National Book Critics Circle Award in 2023._
